mass_kg.note: No published body mass for Roman soldiers found for this fighter; category default (estimate 1 of 3, allowed by D-54).

source.title: Human height
source.quote: The Romans were slightly taller, with an average height of 169 cm (5 ft 7 in) for males and 158 cm (5 ft 2 in) for females.

size_m.note: Average height of Roman men generally, not soldiers specifically. Range is the standard +/-10%.

top_speed_mps.note: No published sprint speed for an armored soldier found for this fighter; category default (estimate 2 of 3, allowed by D-54).

source.title: Forces generated in stabbing attacks (Nolan, Hainsworth and Rutty 2017, Int. J. Legal Med. 132:229)
source.quote: for an unrestrained stab by a man, using their dominant hand, the mean peak force generated was approximately 150 N for pork thigh

attack_force_n.note: Stand-in for a gladius thrust: untrained volunteers stabbing with knives, not soldiers with swords. Range is +/-25%.

attacks_per_s.note: No published sword strike rate found for this fighter; category default (estimate 3 of 3, allowed by D-54).

source.title: Gladius
source.quote: Gladii that have been found measured 425–590 mm in length, 36–90 mm in width, and weighed between 1.2 and 1.6 kg.

reach_m.note: The sword's length, counted as reach (docs/research.md: a published weapon length counts). Upper figure of the found Mainz-type gladii (late 1st century BC to late 1st century AD); the source gives no mean.

armor_0_1.note: armor level 4: metal body armor and a large shield.

source.title: Gladiator
source.quote: most bouts would have lasted 10 to 15 minutes, or 20 minutes at most.

endurance_s.note: Stand-in: the length of a gladiator bout, a fighting duration (allowed by the PM on #29). Upper typical figure; low and high are the source's 10 and 20 minutes. Bout length for gladiators generally; heavily armed fighters tired faster, so this may overstate a legionary's stamina.

aggression_0_1.note: aggression level 4: trained soldier, confident against most opponents.

group_tactics_0_1.note: group tactics level 5: drilled unit acting as one (the rubric's own example).
